review_notes: The file is five generated proof-term declarations. I read the structure, the three split_alpha certificates and the junctions where their halves repeat. I checked the definitions behind them: freshVar, mem_lt_freshVar and the TAlphaWff constructors. I did not read every line of the roughly 3800-line terms. I did not check whether other Part files repeat the same pattern. I could not run Lean, so the proposed helpers and rewrites are uncompiled. The `ne_freshVar_of_mem` rewrite assumes `exact` can unfold `nb095AlphaDummyNNN` by delta, which I did not verify. I checked that the second half of each term has the same shape as the first half. I did not check every inner subterm. The repeated 19-entry `reflOfClosed` environment lists are also a large source of duplication, but they are data, not reasoning, so I did not report them.

findings.problem: All three certificates prove a statement of the form `Wff.imp P (Wff.neg P)` against `Wff.imp P' (Wff.neg P')`. Each is written as `TAlphaWff.imp X (TAlphaWff.neg X)`, with the roughly 600-line alpha-equivalence derivation X pasted twice. In 0073 the first copy is before line 648 and the second is lines 649-1236. In 0074 the second copy starts at 1938 and in 0075 at 3228. Each copy repeats the same freshness side-proofs, `reflOfClosed` environments and `TAlphaVar.there` chains. Only line breaking differs. The same term is therefore elaborated twice, and any edit must be made in two places. It is also hard to see that the two halves agree.
findings.proposed_change: Add a small combinator next to `TAlphaWff` in NominalAlphaTransport.lean: `def TAlphaWff.impNegSelf {env : TBinderEnv} {p p' : Wff} (h : TAlphaWff env p p') : TAlphaWff env (Wff.imp p (Wff.neg p)) (Wff.imp p' (Wff.neg p')) := TAlphaWff.imp h (TAlphaWff.neg h)`. Its proof just reuses `h` in both slots. Then rewrite each certificate as `TAlphaWff.impNegSelf (TAlphaWff.classMem (TAlphaClass.cv (TAlphaVar.here _ _ _)) (TAlphaClass.cab ...))`, writing the large `classMem` derivation once. This applies to 0073 (the derivation up to line 647), 0074 (up to line 1937) and 0075 (up to line 3226). The environment, `P` and `P'` are unchanged, so the declared types stay the same. As a fallback, the derivation can be bound once with `let X := ...` or `have`.
findings.benefit: This roughly halves each of the three huge terms and removes about 1,900 lines. It states the intent, `A → ¬A`, in one place. The term is elaborated once, and later regeneration or repair of the nominal side conditions touches one copy instead of two.

findings.problem: There are 317 repeats of one inline argument: `show (a) ≠ (b) from (by unfold b; with_reducible exact (Nat.ne_of_lt (mem_lt_freshVar (nb095_support_mem_NNNN ...) k)))`. Here `b` is a `freshVar` of a support set containing `a`, with offset `k`. Each one re-derives that a variable is not equal to a fresh variable built from a support containing it, using `mem_lt_freshVar` and `Nat.ne_of_lt`. `ReplaySupport.Basic` has `mem_lt_freshVar` and `freshVar_injective`, but no lemma stating `x ∈ support → x ≠ freshVar support k`. The step is therefore rewritten by hand in every `TAlphaVar.there`.
findings.proposed_change: Add to ReplaySupport/Basic.lean: `theorem ne_freshVar_of_mem {support : Finset Var} {x : Var} (hx : x ∈ support) (offset : Nat := 0) : x ≠ freshVar support offset := Nat.ne_of_lt (mem_lt_freshVar hx offset)`. Then each occurrence becomes `(show (nb095AlphaDummy098 D R S_cls E) ≠ (nb095AlphaDummy105 D R S_cls E) from ne_freshVar_of_mem (nb095_support_mem_0090 D R S_cls E) 0)`. The `unfold` is no longer needed because `exact` elaborates up to delta. I did not compile this. If `exact` does not unfold the abbreviation, keep a single `by unfold ...; exact` per site.
findings.benefit: Each 6-line block shrinks to one expression. Fewer than 1,900 lines of boilerplate remain in this file. The ordering fact is stated once, and the intent (a fresh variable differs from variables in its support) is visible. If `freshVar` changes, one lemma needs fixing, not 317 call sites.
